question: Which mechanism BEST explains how the HPV oncoprotein E6 contributes to cervical carcinogenesis?

answers.text: E6 binds and degrades p53 via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, preventing apoptosis of HPV-infected cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: E6 recruits E6-AP (E6-associated protein), a cellular E3 ubiquitin ligase, to target p53 for proteasomal degradation. Loss of p53 — the 'guardian of the genome' — eliminates the apoptotic response to DNA damage, allowing genomically unstable HPV-infected cells to survive and proliferate.

answers.text: E6 binds and inactivates Rb, releasing E2F transcription factors for uncontrolled cell cycle entry

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Rb inactivation and E2F release is the function of E7, not E6. Remember: E6 targets p53 (apoptosis checkpoint) and E7 targets Rb (cell cycle checkpoint) — two distinct tumour suppressor pathways disabled by two different oncoproteins.

answers.text: E6 integrates viral DNA into the c-MYC proto-oncogene locus, causing its overexpression

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: c-MYC translocation — specifically t(8;14) — is associated with Burkitt's lymphoma driven by EBV, not HPV. HPV E6 does not cause insertional activation of proto-oncogenes; its mechanism is p53 degradation via the ubiquitin pathway.

answers.text: E6 binds the CD21 receptor on B lymphocytes, triggering polyclonal B-cell activation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CD21 (complement receptor type 2) is the receptor for Epstein-Barr virus on B cells. EBV uses CD21 for B-cell entry and can drive B-cell lymphomas. HPV does not interact with CD21; it infects squamous epithelial cells.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the HPV oncoproteins carefully: E6 targets p53 for ubiquitin-mediated degradation, E7 targets Rb for inactivation. These two mechanisms are frequently confused — keep them distinct: E6 → p53, E7 → Rb.

Correct! The E6-E7 pair works in tandem: E6 destroys p53 (preventing apoptosis) while E7 destroys Rb (releasing E2F for uncontrolled cell division). High-risk HPV 16 and 18 expressing both oncoproteins simultaneously disable the two critical tumour suppressor pathways.
